scope.activation: issuer allowlist claim_schemas and optional trusted runner startup argument

proof_state.v1: trusted issuer signature binds the current input and structural manifest; it does not bind mutable layer state
proof_state.v2: trusted issuer signature also binds active_state_checkpoint_bytes_sha256 for the exact stateful multi-input ProgramBundle bytes
proof_state.active_state_checkpoint_bytes_sha256: the Node host computes SHA-256 from the current graph and registry; its digest is surfaced in host_provenance when an issuer allows v2
proof_state.state_freshness: v2 digest is checked at bind and rechecked before run, verify, and checkpoint operations
proof_state.execution_replay: the same current claims may be used for repeated execution while the active checkpoint bytes remain unchanged; v2 is state freshness binding, not one-shot execution authorization
proof_state.receipt: v2 execution receipts preserve the claim schema and state digest for each v2 input while retaining the existing v1 input projection; a receipt-level common digest is present when every input uses the same state-bound digest
proof_state.authority: Node host transport gate only; Burn remains numerical reference authority

canonical_claim_v2.encoding: UTF-8 bytes of JSON.stringify in canonicalInputClaim insertion order, followed by active_state_checkpoint_bytes_sha256
canonical_claim_v2.signature: Ed25519 detached signature encoded as canonical base64
canonical_claim_v2.digest_format: sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
canonical_claim_v2.digest_scope: exact exported multi-input ProgramBundle bytes including structural identity and mutable layer state

issuer_policy.state_bound_required_mode: every configured issuer must allow v2 and every runtime input must carry a current v2 claim

valid_transitions: a host with an issuer that allows v2 exposes the active checkpoint digest without exporting raw state bytes
bind verifies the issuer allowlist, exact canonical claim, current checkpoint digest, subject, nonce, and increasing revision before mutating the input bundle
run, verify, and checkpoint re-hash the active state before operating on v2-bound inputs
durable receipts carry per-input state digests and distinguish them from the post-execution state_checkpoint_bytes_sha256
legacy v1 issuers and hosts retain the existing v1 behavior unless state-bound mode is required
limits: A checkpoint digest binds bytes and state freshness; it does not authenticate checkpoint origin, establish semantic state equivalence, or authorize actions.
A claim nonce prevents rebinding the same claim, but does not limit repeated runs over the same still-current claim set.
The trust policy and issuer private keys remain controlled outside the JSON Lines caller.
A privileged writer of the host ledger can rewrite its history; receipt IDs remain content digests rather than digital signatures.
Direct callers of exported WASM APIs can bypass the Node host gate.
The active state digest can reveal equality or correlation between serialized states; the host never returns raw checkpoint bytes through this field.
